title: 5.9.6 Lab: Hit the drone
description: Shots fly straight through the falling drone. Use overlaps() so a shot that touches it scores, leaves the screen and the array, and sends the drone back to the top.

steps.title: The shot that hits leaves
steps.instructions: The drone falls from the top, and the starter sends it back up when it reaches the base. Your work is all in `hitDrone()`, which already loops backwards over `bullets`. Inside the loop, test `bullets[i].overlaps(drone)`. When it is true, delete the shot and splice it out of `bullets` on that same frame: `overlaps()` stays true on every frame the two touch, so a shot left in place would keep hitting.
hints: Inside the braces: `bullets[i].delete();` then `bullets.splice(i, 1);`, the same two lines `moveBullets()` uses.

steps.title: A hit scores and resets the drone
steps.instructions: In the same if, add 1 to `score` and call `resetDrone()`, which puts the drone back above the top at a random x. Play: each shot that lands should add exactly 1, and the drone should jump straight back to the top.
hints: `score += 1;` and `resetDrone();` go after the splice, inside the same braces.
If the score climbs while nothing is touching the drone, `score += 1` has ended up outside the if.

requirements.title: overlaps is used on the drone
requirements.description: Each shot asks overlaps(drone) on every frame. Help: 5.9.5 (Reading: Did the shot hit?)

requirements.title: The shot that hit leaves the screen and the array
requirements.description: Inside the overlaps if, the shot is deleted and spliced out of bullets on the frame it hits. Help: 5.9.5 (Reading: Did the shot hit?)

requirements.title: A hit scores 1 and resets the drone
requirements.description: Inside the same if, score goes up by 1 and the drone goes back to the top. Help: 5.9.5 (Reading: Did the shot hit?)
